todaysEvents.delta: Up: Axios (Jul 9) reports US strikes on Iranian Hormuz targets for a second straight day to degrade threats to navigation.
Up: AP (Jul 9) reports Iran struck US military infrastructure in three Gulf states after renewed American attacks.
Down: Axios (Jul 9) reports Qatar, Pakistan and regional mediators are trying to revive negotiations and prevent a return to all-out war.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Qatar and Pakistan secure a new pause after the ceasefire's collapse. Iran stops further attacks, US strikes remain limited, and monitored corridors reopen in phases. Brent holds $72-82/bbl as shipping resumes unevenly and Ras Laffan recovery remains late-August at best. Probability cut to 40% after a second day of US strikes and Iranian retaliation.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Continued limited exchanges keep Hormuz traffic constrained while mediation proceeds. US patrols and strikes contain immediate threats, but insurers price high-risk transit. Brent trades $78-95/bbl, JKM holds $18-22/MMBtu, iTraxx Asia IG widens toward 145bp, and ASEAN importers hedge freight and fuel exposure.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: The retaliation cycle broadens. Iran attacks or seizes more vessels, US strikes deepen, and mediation fails before nuclear talks resume. Hormuz remains militarised; Brent spikes $115-140/bbl and LNG risk premia surge. Probability raised to 22% after second-day US strikes and Iranian retaliation across Gulf states.
